alz_001.text: Donepezil is a cholinesterase inhibitor approved for mild to severe Alzheimer's disease. It improves cognition by increasing acetylcholine availability.
Memantine (Namenda) is an NMDA receptor antagonist used for moderate to severe AD. It works differently from cholinesterase inhibitors.
Late-stage Alzheimer's care focuses on palliative comfort measures, pain management, and maintaining quality of life.

alz_002.text: Amyloid beta peptides aggregate into insoluble plaques that accumulate extracellularly in the Alzheimer's brain.
Tau hyperphosphorylation causes neurofibrillary tangles, disrupting axonal transport in neurons.

alz_003.text: Regular aerobic exercise has been shown to reduce Alzheimer's disease risk by improving cerebrovascular health.
The Mediterranean diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids and antioxidants is associated with reduced cognitive decline.
Cognitive engagement through education and mental stimulation builds cognitive reserve against AD pathology.

alz_004.text: The APOE4 allele is the strongest known genetic risk factor for late-onset sporadic Alzheimer's disease.
APOE4 heterozygotes have 3-4x increased risk; homozygotes have 8-12x increased risk of developing AD.

alz_005.text: The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) is a widely used screening tool for cognitive impairment in Alzheimer's.
MRI brain imaging reveals hippocampal atrophy characteristic of Alzheimer's disease progression.
CSF biomarkers including amyloid-42, total tau, and phospho-tau are used in AD diagnosis.

alz_006.text: Acetylcholine is a neurotransmitter critical for memory and learning, deficient in Alzheimer's disease.
Donepezil inhibits acetylcholinesterase, preventing breakdown of acetylcholine and temporarily improving memory.

alz_007.text: Early-onset Alzheimer's (before age 65) accounts for about 5% of cases and is often linked to APP, PSEN1, or PSEN2 mutations.
Late-onset Alzheimer's is primarily sporadic with genetic susceptibility from APOE4 and environmental factors.

alz_008.text: Activated microglia surround amyloid plaques and release pro-inflammatory cytokines including TNF-alpha and IL-1beta.
Chronic neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease contributes to progressive neuronal loss and cognitive decline.

str_001.text: The FAST acronym (Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time) is the primary public awareness tool for stroke recognition.
Ischemic stroke presents with sudden onset of neurological deficits depending on the affected brain region.

str_002.text: Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) is the only FDA-approved thrombolytic for ischemic stroke treatment.
The treatment window for intravenous tPA is 4.5 hours from symptom onset in eligible patients.

str_003.text: Hypertension is the leading cause of hemorrhagic stroke through vessel wall weakening and rupture.
Intracranial aneurysm rupture causes subarachnoid hemorrhage with characteristic sudden severe headache.

str_004.text: Post-stroke physiotherapy focuses on regaining motor function through neuroplasticity-based exercises.
Speech and language therapy addresses post-stroke aphasia and dysphagia for communication and swallowing recovery.

gen_001.text: Machine learning algorithms learn patterns from training data to make predictions on new unseen data.
Supervised learning uses labeled examples; unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data.

gen_002.text: Neural networks consist of input, hidden, and output layers with weighted connections between neurons.
Backpropagation adjusts weights by computing gradients of the loss function with respect to each parameter.

gen_003.text: Knowledge graphs represent entities as nodes and edges forming a semantic network.
Graph databases like Neo4j store and query knowledge graph data using Cypher query language.

gen_004.text: Transformer models use self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies in text sequences.
Word embeddings map tokens to dense vector spaces where semantic similarity corresponds to geometric proximity.

edge_002.text: Pizza toppings are a matter of personal preference with no medical significance.
